answer.worked: Graph III extends across every $x$-value. Its minimum $y$-value is $1$, which is included, and its arms continue upwards without bound. Match: (III).
Graph IV extends across every $x$-value. It stays above $y=1$, approaching this horizontal asymptote without reaching it, and continues upwards without bound. Match: (IV).
The circle in graph VI reaches $x=-1$, $x=1$, $y=-1$ and $y=1$. Its projections cover both closed intervals $[-1,1]$. Match: (VI).
Graph II lies strictly to the right of the vertical asymptote $x=1$. Its $y$-values extend without bound in both directions. Match: (II).
Graph I has leftmost point $(1,0)$, so $x=1$ is included and the graph extends to the right. Its two branches give every real $y$-value. Match: (I).
Graph V runs from the filled point $(-1,1)$ to the filled point $(1,0)$. Its horizontal projection is $[-1,1]$ and its vertical projection is $[0,1]$, including all endpoints. Match: (V).
